item.title: Asahikawa Winter Festival Guide: Snow Sculptures & Zoo
item.description: Hokkaido’s second city, Asahikawa, is one of Japan’s coldest places — and it embraces winter wholeheartedly. Each February, the Asahikawa Winter Festival raises some of the largest snow sculptures in Japan (it has held world records), with huge snow stages, slides and illuminations along the Ishikari River and downtown. The city is also home to the wildly popular Asahiyama Zoo, famous for its winter penguin walk, and is a hub for Asahikawa-style soy ramen and a gateway to the Daisetsuzan mountains.

item.title: Sapporo Snow Festival Guide: Dates, Sites & Tips (Feb)
item.description: The Sapporo Snow Festival (Yuki Matsuri) is Japan’s biggest and most famous winter event, drawing millions to Hokkaido’s capital each February. For about a week, Odori Park becomes a glittering open-air gallery of colossal snow sculptures — towering castles, temples and pop-culture characters — alongside delicate ice sculptures in Susukino and a family snow-play zone at the Tsudome. After dark, the sculptures are spectacularly lit up and projection-mapped. With street food, hot drinks and a magical atmosphere, it’s a bucket-list winter experience.
